quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should motorcycle pants be made of to protect a rider?

options.text: Loose fabric that flaps in the wind
Short pants that expose the legs

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy material
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy material. They should cover your entire legs and fit snugly without flapping in the wind. They should also not be so tight that they restrict movement.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the other driver will yield to you
It is not worth the effort
It does not mean the driver will yield to you
It means the other driver knows you are there

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean the driver will yield to you
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will give you the right-of-way. Do not count on it for your safety.

questions.question: When should you use both brakes on a motorcycle?

options.text: Only when the road is wet
Every time you slow down or stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you slow down or stop
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do before downshifting when going downhill?

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down first
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down first
questions.explanation: Slow your motorcycle to a safe speed before downshifting. If you downshift too fast, the motorcycle may jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to increase your visibility as a rider?

options.text: Use your headlight at all times

questions.correctAnswerText: Wave at other drivers
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight all the time, and use your turn signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider be ready for when passing parked cars?

options.text: A car suddenly pulling out into traffic
Other drivers seeing the motorcycle and staying out of the way

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out into traffic
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out without warning. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space to avoid a car that suddenly pulls out.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular, white with black lettering. They tell you the rules you must follow on the road.

questions.question: A good lane position helps with all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them with saddlebags. Do not pile items on the sissy bar. High loads change the motorcycle's balance and center of gravity. Loads must be balanced equally on both sides.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible across the slippery surface.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: one in front, one in back, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Why should you use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake will cause the brakes to wear unevenly.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
Using both brakes is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops helps you develop a habit. This habit will be critical in emergencies when you may need both brakes to stop safely.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you the best view of the passing lane ahead.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can slow down by downshifting. Be aware that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you apply the brakes?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always apply both brakes at the same time every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while you are riding, what happens?

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire will cause the steering to feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull over right away and check your tires.

questions.question: You may need less following distance if:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions are not perfect. You need more space if the pavement is slippery, you can't see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Your body processes about one drink per hour. If someone drinks seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks will be in their system three hours after the last drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To find remaining drinks, subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. A person who drank seven drinks in three hours would have four drinks remaining in their system three hours later.

questions.question: Night riding:

options.text: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces provide poor grip for motorcycle tires. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you may need to adjust:
questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks to handle this weight. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has curved mirrors, why should you practice using them?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors give you a wider view of the road behind you. However, they make objects seem farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: Before passing another rider on the left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane so they can see you in their mirror.
Move to the left side of your lane to see ahead better.
Stay in the center of your lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave side to side in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left side of your lane to see ahead better.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, move to the left side of your lane. This helps you see ahead and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: In a normal turn, what should the motorcycle and rider do?

options.text: The motorcycle leans; the rider stays upright.
The rider leans; the motorcycle stays upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean together.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider keeps their body upright.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake supply?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: When you need to stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Press hard on the front brake to prevent the tire from skidding.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, how should they do it?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before passing. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When there are only a few vehicles on the road.
When drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space between you and the vehicle ahead if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance when the road is slippery, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT protect you in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose clothing made of strong, durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: You could be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because it limits your escape routes.
It should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Never ride directly beside another vehicle because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. They could change lanes into you without warning. Riding beside a vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If your motorcycle wobbles, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and move your weight down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Avoid braking, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing and gear to make sure other drivers can see you and your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding beside a car?

options.text: You could be in a blind spot.
It is only a problem when the road is wet.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could be in a blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle also blocks your path of escape.

questions.question: How should you brake on a slippery road?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or strong material, boots that cover and support your ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts to rain?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is dangerous when wet. When rain starts, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: If your motorcycle wobbles, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding, as it will likely stop on its own.
Slowly close the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will only make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can and check what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: Why check your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: Only a mechanic can do a useful check.
You should never check it before riding.
Check it only after you ride.
It helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you spot problems that could hurt you.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of these, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid hazards and blind spots. It tells other drivers your plans and gives you room to escape danger. It does not help you avoid traffic signals.

questions.question: Which gives the best face protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What reduces your risk of a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Watch only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to avoid hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible. Use turn signals and your brake light. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be ready to avoid danger.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Cut their space cushions in half.
Keep enough space around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only use your mirrors to check for vehicles.
Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
Brake hard so vehicles in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is safest to:

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to cross at a right angle may push you into another lane.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to escape the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up—it makes wobbling worse. Hold the handlebars firm, slowly reduce speed, and lean forward. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: Making eye contact with a driver:

options.text: Guarantees they will let you go.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact. A driver may look right at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: Which does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol was consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often you drink alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol you drank, how fast you drank it, and your body weight. Gender, health, and food intake also matter. How often you drink does not affect your current BAC.
